Article Title: Megan Thee Stallion’s foundation helped Mila launch a mental health project with a $550 grant; after starting in 2024, her nonprofit reports delivering more than 2,200 care packages to Black girls
Article Text:
How a personal struggle inspired MH Boxes

The $550 grant that helped turn the idea into a nonprofit

From 500 packages to more than 3,300

Why representation matters in mental health support

A $550 grant helped a 12-year-old girl turn her own mental health struggles into a project that has since reached thousands of others. Mila Henry launched MH Boxes in January 2024 after receiving a microgrant through the #BlackGirlJoyChallenge, an initiative backed by rapper Megan Thee Stallion ’s Pete & Thomas Foundation and the Southern Black Girls & Women’s Consortium. What began as a small effort to support Black girls facing mental health challenges has grown into a nonprofit that now reports delivering 3,303 care packages across 17 states and Washington, DC, according to its official website.The boxes contain journals, fidget toys, affirmations and other self-care tools designed to help Black girls feel supported and encourage conversations about mental health. The project draws on Mila’s own experiences and her belief that young people facing emotional difficulties should have access to resources that recognise their needs and make them feel less alone. The initiative also highlights how relatively small grants can help young people turn personal experiences into community-led projects.Mila came up with the idea after experiencing anxiety and receiving mental health treatment herself. In a May 2024 profile, Richmond Family Magazine reported that she had struggled with anxiety and depression during middle school and had been hospitalised for mental health treatment towards the end of the Covid-19 pandemic.Her experience helped her recognise that other girls might also need encouragement and practical resources when dealing with emotional difficulties.The care packages were designed specifically for Black girls, who Mila and her family believed were not always adequately represented in conversations about mental health. The boxes include tactile items such as slime, modelling clay and fidget toys, alongside journals, handmade bracelets, positive messages and information about mental health resources. The aim is not to replace professional treatment, but to offer reassurance and tools that can make it easier for girls to acknowledge their feelings and seek support.Mila initially distributed the boxes through educators, mental health providers, schools and community organisations in central Virginia. By May 2024, Richmond Family Magazine reported that she had delivered more than 500 packages.The project received an early boost through the #BlackGirlJoyChallenge, a collaboration between the Pete & Thomas Foundation and the Southern Black Girls & Women’s Consortium. The initiative was created to help young Black women develop community projects focused on mental health, wellness and spreading joy. In its 2024 edition, 100 young women received $550 microgrants to put their ideas into action.Mila used her grant to establish MH Boxes in January 2024. The project subsequently developed into a nonprofit organisation focused on providing culturally affirming mental health support to Black girls. The Pete & Thomas Foundation was established in 2022 in honour of Megan Thee Stallion’s late parents. Its work includes supporting initiatives involving education, housing and health and wellness in underserved communities.The grant programme illustrates how funding can help young people move beyond an idea and establish projects that respond to needs they have experienced themselves.MH Boxes has continued expanding since its launch. In July 2025, Axios reported that Mila had distributed 1,600 boxes across five states. The report also noted that Megan Thee Stallion praised Mila’s work when the teenager received the Pete & Thomas Foundation’s Young Humanitarian Award at an event in New York.The nonprofit’s website now lists 3,303 mental health boxes delivered to Black girls across 17 states and Washington, DC. Its impact page had previously reported that more than 2,200 packages had reached girls during the organisation’s first year.The figures indicate the project's reported growth from a local effort into a wider initiative. The packages reach girls through schools, community partners and families, helping extend the project beyond its original distribution network.MH Boxes also says its work is expanding beyond the physical packages. Its broader vision includes youth leadership, advocacy, peer support and efforts to help Black girls participate in decisions affecting their mental health.The organisation says its work is intended to address stigma and barriers that can prevent Black girls from accessing or discussing mental health support. Its packages are designed with their intended recipients in mind, combining practical items with messages that affirm their worth and encourage them to talk about difficult feelings. By including information about mental health resources, the initiative also aims to help girls and families identify additional avenues of support.The need for such resources extends beyond the boxes themselves. Mental health care can involve professional counselling, treatment and support from families, schools and communities. MH Boxes positions its packages as one part of that wider network rather than a substitute for clinical care.The organisation's next phase includes building youth leadership opportunities and developing programmes intended to help Black girls influence mental health policy and access pathways into mental health careers.
Article Summary: MH Boxes was founded by 12-year-old Mila Henry after receiving a $550 microgrant through the #BlackGirlJoyChallenge. The initiative was created to help young Black women develop community projects focused on mental health, wellness and spreading joy. Mila used her grant to establish MH Boxes in January 2024. The project subsequently developed into a nonprofit organisation focused on providing culturally affirming mental health support to Black girls. The organisation now reports delivering 3,303 care packages across 17 states and Washington, DC, according to its official website.

Article Title: 'Trump will take his dream to his grave': Iran determined to not allow US warships in Hormuz
Article Text:
“We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time,” Chief of staff of Iran’s armed forces, Ali Abdollahi, said (Photo: ANI).

Possible strike on Iran this weekend?

Iran on Saturday vowed not to allow US military ships into the Persian Gulf “under any circumstances”, as tensions with Washington escalated amid threats of further military action by the United States.Iran's armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi remarked after US President Donald Trump threatened another "little Epic Fury" to force Iran's compliance, in case negotiations fail.“We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time,” Iranian state television quoted the chief of staff of Iran’s armed forces, Ali Abdollahi, as saying. AFP reported.“The US president must dream of seeing the armed forces enter the Persian Gulf. He will take that dream to his grave,” Abdollahi added.Iranian forces have restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key energy route connecting the Gulf to the wider world, since the war with the United States began on February 28. In response, Washington has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and vessels.Tehran has required ships to obtain permission to transit the strait and has repeatedly targeted vessels attempting to pass through a southern route near the Omani coast.According to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, several tankers attempting to use the route, which Tehran considers “illegal”, have been hit by mines in recent days.On Friday, the Guards said two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil had been abandoned at sea after striking mines in the strategic waterway. AFP reported.The latest warning from Tehran came after US Ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack said on Friday that a US strike on Iran could take place over the weekend, while stressing that Trump remained open to a diplomatic agreement.“Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely,” Barrack said in an interview with Lebanese-Australian entrepreneur Mario Nawfal on Friday.Barrack, who also serves as Trump’s special envoy, said the US president remained willing to negotiate but warned that continued threats against the United States, its allies and Gulf countries would have consequences.“The president has been clear. I'm giving you American policy. President is very clear. He's open and available and accessible to a deal. And we've been at the table for months and months and months,” Barrack said.Hours later, Trump addressed a rally in Florida where he told Americans that the possibility of further military action was open.“We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree,” Trump said.“If they're smart, they'll just say, 'Let's get down to business.' But, you know, I doubt they'll do that because perhaps they're not smart,” he added.
Article Summary: “We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time,” Iranian state television quoted the chief of staff of Iran’s armed forces, Ali Abdollahi, as saying. US President Donald Trump threatened another "little Epic Fury" to force Iran's compliance, in case negotiations fail.

Article Title: In 2012, Josh Hutcherson bought a Hollywood Hills hideaway once owned by Heath Ledger for $2.5 million; eight years later, the 1951 home with a 2,500-square-foot deck sold for $2.94 million
Article Text:
Pic credit: Chron

A home with famous owners

Pic credit: Wral.com

Inside the retreat-like home

Pic credit: People

The deck

Pic credit: Chron

Pic credit: People

Pic credit: AD

Some homes boast standout features; others have stories etched into their walls. Josh Hutcherson ’s former Hollywood Hills hideaway had both. Built in 1951, the secluded Midcentury Modern home is a perfect retreat and has a few famous names in its history. Tucked behind heavy landscaping, this secluded home has had several famous owners, from Ellen DeGeneres and Heath Ledger to Josh Hutcherson himself. Josh Hutcherson bought the half-acre, wood-clad Hollywood gem in 2012 for $2.94 million. In 2019, he sold the home for $2.94 million, the Los Angeles Times reports.The house sits behind thick landscaping, so most people driving past never see it. That’s one of the reasons why famous people have consistently sought it out. The Hunger Games actor Josh Hutcherson bought the property through a trust in 2012, according to public records. He was not the first well-known name on the deed. Talk-show host Ellen DeGeneres bought the house for $1.3 million and later sold it to actor Heath Ledger for $2.3 million, the Daily Mail reported. After Ledger’s death, his estate sold the home for $2.5 million. Furniture designer Guy Chaddock also lived in the secluded Hollywood Hills home at some point.The Midcentury Modern home spans nearly 1,900 square feet, with two bedrooms and two bathrooms, People reported. Polished concrete floors run through the home, and beamed ceilings sit overhead. A fireplace and brick wall fill the far end of the living room.Glass doors open from that room onto the outdoor deck.The kitchen has been updated with modern stainless-steel Miele and Sub-Zero appliances, plus a wine fridge. A small office and reading nook sit just off the kitchen area. The layout is simple, and that seems to be the point. The house was built for quiet days and easy movement between the rooms and the outdoors.The outdoor area is where the home really stretches out. The deck adds about 2,500 square feet of living space, according to the listing. It includes a sunken conversation pit and a lounge area with a drop-down projector. The space also has an outdoor grill and a screening room.The deck looks over a private, wooded hillside. No wonder the home is often called a ‘tree house’. For a property of this size, that view does a lot of the selling!The home was listed for about $3.5 million, according to the Daily Mail. It sold for $2.94 million, a figure close to what Hutcherson paid eight years earlier. The sale brought the property’s price history full circle, at least in terms of what he got back.Deedee Howard and Charlie Heydt of The Agency were the listing agents. Paul Salazar of Hilton & Hyland represented the buyer.For the buyer, the house offers a perfect retreat and privacy. Its 1951 bones remain intact, with original features such as the beamed ceilings and fireplace wall. The updated kitchen and appliances make it easier to live in day to day. The property also carries the names of its previous famous owners. Each owner has added a chapter to its story, and the next buyer will inherit that history along with the wood, concrete and glass!
Article Summary: Josh Hutcherson bought the half-acre, wood-clad Hollywood gem in 2012 for $2.94 million. Talk-show host Ellen DeGeneres bought the house for $1.3 million and later sold it to actor Heath Ledger for $3.5 million. Furniture designer Guy Chaddock also lived in the secluded Hollywood Hills home at some point.

Article Title: American artist Mark Cline recreated Stonehenge using foam in 2004; after more than a decade at Natural Bridge, Virginia, the life-sized replica found a new home at a farm
Article Text:
PC: Cox Farms

Foamhenge began as a life-sized Stonehenge replica in 2004

Stonehenge replica seeks relocation after years at Natural Bridge

From Natural Bridge to Cox Farms, Stonehenge replica finds a new home

Cox Farms sets seasonal visiting hours for the Stonehenge replica

An American artist recreated Stonehenge using foam rather than ancient stone, building a life-sized replica that made its debut on April Fool’s Day in 2004. Known as Foamhenge, the installation was created by Mark Cline of Enchanted Castle Studio and stood in Natural Bridge, Virginia, for more than a decade.In 2016, Cline said the site was due to become part of Natural Bridge State Park and that the replica needed a new home. The attraction eventually moved to Cox Farms in Centreville, Virginia, where it made its debut at the farm’s Fall Festival in 2017. Cox Farms says visitors can see Foamhenge during specified seasonal hours or the Fall Festival.Mark Cline created Foamhenge through his company, Enchanted Castle Studio, in a business partnership with the Natural Bridge site to attract more tourists to the area. It is made from styrofoam; the replica recreated England’s famous Stonehenge monument and made its debut on April Fool’s Day in 2004. The unusual installation drew visitors from around the world, according to ABC News. Foamhenge was not Cline’s only Stonehenge replica. He also built a second version in Josephine, Alabama, making the Virginia attraction one of two such installations associated with the artist.In May 2016, Foamhenge stood on land that was set to become part of Natural Bridge State Park.Cline said he was disappointed the park did not see the replica’s value, but acknowledged it had remained at the site for more than a decade, longer than he expected.Cline planned to give Foamhenge away, provided it was moved before August 1. The recipient would have to cover the cost of dismantling the installation and reassembling it at a new site. Cline also hoped the replica would find a home where it could continue attracting visitors and benefit the surrounding area.Foamhenge later found a new home at Cox Farms in Centreville, Virginia. The farm says the installation made its debut there in 2017 as part of its Fall Festival. Before that move, it had stood in Natural Bridge, where it was first installed in 2004. Cox Farms identifies Mark Cline of Enchanted Castle Studio as the artist who created it.The relocation gave the life-sized replica a place within the farm’s attraction programme. Foamhenge is on private property, according to Cox Farms, and access depends on the season and scheduled opening times. Visitors should check the farm’s information before planning a visit, as access is not available at all times throughout the year.Cox Farms says access to Foamhenge is included with admission during the Fall Festival’s regular operating hours. Foamhenge has limited visiting hours beyond the autumn festival. For spring and summer 2026, Cox Farms listed access from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m. on Saturdays between April 24 and August 16, as part of its weekly Smokin’ Saturday events. Visitors could reach the installation by shuttle from the Corner Market during these hours. In fall 2026, the replica is included with Fall Festival admission and can be visited during the farm’s regular operating hours.
Article Summary: Foamhenge was created by Mark Cline of Enchanted Castle Studio in 2004. It stood in Natural Bridge, Virginia, for more than a decade. In 2016, Cline said the site was due to become part of Natural Bridge State Park and that the replica needed a new home. The attraction eventually moved to Cox Farms in Centreville, Virginia. It made its debut at the farm’s Fall Festival in 2017.

Article Title: Colorado built a giant green bridge over a busy highway for animals; wildlife-vehicle collisions fell by 91% as they found a safer way across
Article Text:
Colorado's giant green wildlife bridge over Interstate 25

Wildlife-vehicle collisions fell by 91%

Why elk and pronghorn need a bridge instead of a tunnel

Elk and pronghorn have begun using the crossing

The $15 million project connects 39,000 acres of habitat

Researchers will study whether the bridge reconnects wildlife populations

Colorado's wildlife crossings offer a model for safer roads

A grass-covered bridge spanning six lanes of a busy US highway is helping wildlife cross safely between habitats, while a wider network of crossings and fences has cut animal-vehicle collisions by 91% along a stretch of Interstate 25 in Colorado. The Greenland Wildlife Overpass, completed in December 2025, connects 39,000 acres of habitat near Larkspur and Monument, south of Denver. The $15 million structure is designed primarily for large animals such as elk and pronghorn, which often avoid enclosed tunnels. It forms part of an 18-mile wildlife-mitigation system that also includes five underpasses and fencing to guide animals away from traffic. State officials say the results offer a promising example of how road infrastructure can protect wildlife while making highways safer for motorists.The Greenland Wildlife Overpass is located near the Greenland interchange in Douglas County, between Larkspur and Monument. Built by the Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT), it spans six lanes of Interstate 25, a major route connecting Denver and Colorado Springs.The bridge measures 200 feet wide and 209 feet long, covering approximately 41,800 square feet. Its surface is layered with soil and vegetation, while its broad, gradually sloping entrances are designed to encourage animals to approach and cross naturally.The structure was completed in December 2025, closing a 3.7-mile gap between existing wildlife crossings along the highway. It connects habitats used by elk, pronghorn, mule deer, black bears and other animals.According to CDOT, the crossing forms part of a wider network designed to reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions and maintain movement between natural habitats separated by the interstate.A state-commissioned study found that wildlife-vehicle collisions along the I-25 South Gap corridor fell by 91% in the final year of the study period. The reduction followed the installation of most of the area's wildlife-mitigation infrastructure, including underpasses and fencing.The corridor previously experienced an average of about one wildlife-vehicle collision per day during periods of high animal movement in spring and autumn. Seasonal migrations bring animals across the landscape as they move between feeding areas and other parts of their ranges.The research examined collision trends from 2022 to 2024. During that period, the average annual reduction was approximately 85%, reaching 91% in the final year.The findings indicate that the wider crossing system has significantly improved safety. However, the overpass itself was completed in December 2025, after the study period, so the 91% figure cannot be attributed solely to the new bridge.Large animals such as elk and pronghorn can be reluctant to enter enclosed passages. Tunnels may restrict their sightlines and movement, while the size of an animal's antlers can make narrow structures particularly unsuitable.The Greenland overpass offers a broad, open route across the highway. Its vegetation-covered surface and gradual approaches are intended to resemble the surrounding landscape, making the crossing more inviting to animals.The wider system complements the bridge with five underpasses that provide alternative routes for wildlife, including smaller species. Fencing along the highway helps guide animals towards these designated crossings rather than allowing them to enter traffic lanes.Together, the measures address two related problems: the risk of collisions and the fragmentation of habitats by major roads.Wildlife cameras have recorded elk herds crossing the overpass, providing early evidence that the structure is being used by the animals it was designed to accommodate.Pronghorn have also been filmed crossing to the western side of I-25. State officials have described these sightings as particularly significant because the highway had long restricted their movement through the area.Monitoring has also recorded smaller wildlife, including rabbits and northern leopard frogs, using the crossing area. The project includes features intended to provide smaller animals with shelter from predators while they move across the exposed bridge.These observations show that the structure is functioning as a wildlife passage. Researchers are continuing to investigate whether it will also help reconnect animal populations that have been separated by the highway.The Greenland overpass cost $15 million to construct, with federal funding providing the bulk of the support through the US Department of Transportation's Wildlife Crossings Pilot Program.The project was developed through cooperation between CDOT, the Federal Highway Administration, Colorado Parks and Wildlife, Douglas County and conservation partners.The crossing connects approximately 39,000 acres of habitat on either side of I-25, with the surrounding wildlife landscape linked to more than one million acres of the Pike National Forest.The overpass also completes a wildlife-crossing network along an 18-mile section of the interstate between Castle Rock and Monument. More than 100,000 vehicles travel through this corridor each day, making the separation between road traffic and animal movement an important safety concern.Reducing collisions is only one measure of the project's success. Researchers also want to understand whether the crossings help animals move between previously separated populations and whether that movement improves genetic diversity over time.Scientists are collecting baseline genetic information from elk populations on both sides of I-25. Comparisons over the coming years are expected to help determine whether the animals are mixing and whether the crossings are improving connectivity between populations.Initial genetic results are expected in spring 2027, with longer-term monitoring needed to assess the effects on wildlife populations.The distinction is important because camera footage can demonstrate that animals use a crossing, but it cannot by itself establish whether populations are becoming more connected or genetically diverse.The Greenland Wildlife Overpass illustrates how transport infrastructure can be designed to accommodate animal movement instead of forcing wildlife to cross busy roads at dangerous points.The decline in collisions across the I-25 corridor suggests that a coordinated system of overpasses, underpasses and fencing can benefit both motorists and wildlife. Fewer collisions can mean less risk of injury, reduced vehicle damage and safer movement for animals travelling between habitats.
Article Summary: The Greenland Wildlife Overpass, completed in December 2025, connects 39,000 acres of habitat near Larkspur and Monument, south of Denver. The $15 million structure is designed primarily for large animals such as elk and pronghorn, which often avoid enclosed tunnels. It forms part of an 18-mile wildlife- mitigation system that also includes five underpasses and fencing to guide animals away from traffic.

Article Title: An Australian builder spent years turning a home for his son into a medieval castle with a moat, a dungeon-style games room and water-spouting gargoyles
Article Text:
Representative Image of a majestic Australian castle-style home with a moat, keep and dungeon-themed games room (AI-generated image)

Why an Australian builder turned a family business headquarters into a medieval castle for his son

Reclaimed church doors, cemetery fencing and an English Axminster carpet add character to the castle

3D-printed gargoyles that release water when it rains complete the unusual castle-style home

A family business needed a headquarters, and Australian builder Ray Hollingsworth had an unconventional solution: build a castle. The result is a three-storey, castle-style home in Warrnambool, Victoria, featuring a moat, a keep, a dungeon-themed games room and gargoyles that release water when it rains. Hollingsworth, who has worked as a builder for more than five decades, built the castle for his eldest son, Richard. It serves as a home for Richard and his wife and as a base for the brothers’ tabletop war-gaming business. ABC News reported on the project in December 2025, noting the family’s shared interest in medieval stories and fantasy.The idea grew out of a practical need. Richard and his brothers run a tabletop war-gaming business, and Hollingsworth thought they needed an appropriate headquarters. He proposed building a castle. The family had long been interested in knights, dragons and medieval fantasy. Richard’s wedding in 2025 also had a medieval theme. Hollingsworth built the property for Richard, his eldest son. The family’s connection to the building extends beyond its construction: the brothers use the basement for their business, while Richard and his wife have made the castle their home. Richard told ABC that the property was a dream come true, both as a place to live and as a base for their work.The project took shape over several years, with the design evolving as construction progressed. Some of its features came from reclaimed materials rather than purpose-made fittings. The entrance incorporates doors sourced from an old church in a nearby town. Wrought-iron fencing recovered from a cemetery was also put to use, while the Axminster carpet had to be brought over from England after a wait of several months. Hollingsworth also received a full suit of armour as a birthday present. The design evolved as the project progressed. Richard told ABC that the keep was a later addition that made the building feel more like a real castle.Hollingsworth said that, because there were no regulations in Australia specifically for a keep, the family had to call the space an attic. This was his explanation, rather than an independently verified statement about Australian building regulations. At the rear of the property is a dungeon-style games room. Fake skeletons hang inside in leg irons and chains from Pentridge Prison, according to ABC. Hollingsworth told ABC that he had never built a moat before and had to learn as he went.Richard’s brother Nicholas designed and 3D-printed the gargoyles, which release water from their mouths when it rains. Hollingsworth, who had worked as a builder for more than five decades, told ABC that this was his first castle. Hollingsworth and Richard are neighbours, reflecting the family’s close ties. Richard and his wife moved into the property a few months before ABC published its report in December 2025. The building’s unusual appearance has the potential to make it a minor tourist attraction, ABC reported, although the article did not establish that it had become a visitor destination. For the family, its main purpose is more personal. The castle provides Richard and his wife with a home, gives the brothers a place to run their tabletop war-gaming business and brings their shared enthusiasm for medieval fantasy into their everyday surroundings. What began as a proposal for a business headquarters became a distinctive castle-style home for Richard and his wife, while also providing space for the brothers’ tabletop war-gaming business.
Article Summary: Australian builder Ray Hollingsworth built a castle for his son Richard. The three-storey home features a moat, a keep, a dungeon-themed games room and gargoyles that release water when it rains. It serves as a home for Richard and his wife and as a base for the brothers’ tabletop war-gaming business.

Article Title: Kim Jong Un photos released to dismiss rumours of coma, takeover by sister
Article Text:
Kim Jong Un inspects pink shoe, women’s coats as death rumours grip North Korea

How the death rumours began

Claims of Chinese troop deployment

What is known about Kim's health?

North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media, inspecting children's footwear and women's clothing, after unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.The photographs, published by North Korea's official media on Monday, show Kim examining footwear, gesturing towards officials and inspecting coats at a garment and footwear exhibition. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis in the secretive country, the New York Post reported.According to North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency, Kim toured the exhibition on Monday. However, the photographs have not been independently authenticated, and it remains unclear precisely when they were taken.One image shows Kim bending forward to inspect a small pink shoe held by a woman. In another, he gestures with his arms outstretched as he appears to address an official. A third photograph captures him reaching towards the sleeve of a woman's coat displayed on a mannequin.The speculation gathered pace after Wanjun Xie, a US-based Chinese dissident associated with the China Democracy Party, posted a series of claims on X alleging that Kim had died and that his sister, Kim Yo Jong , had taken control of the country.In a post on Monday, Xie wrote: "Rumours of the death of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un have been circulating online for days, but Kim Jong Un has not yet made a public appearance to deny them. This indirectly confirms that the rumours of Kim Jong Un's death are likely true. Furthermore, it is rumoured that after Kim Jong-un's death, the North Korean regime has not been transferred to his daughter Kim Ju-ae, but is currently in the hands of his sister Kim Yo-jong."After assuming power, Kim Yo-jong immediately activated loudspeaker broadcasts to South Korea and fired 201 warning shots. She also warned South Korea that North Korea was considering a comprehensive upgrade of its tactical strike capabilities. This sudden intensification of threats against South Korea is clearly aimed at strengthening her control over the North Korean military and consolidating her power through strong external threats. This indirectly confirms the rumors that Kim Jong-un is dead and that Kim Yo-jong is currently in control of the regime; these rumors are likely true."The New York Post reported that Xie's claims began gaining traction on Sunday. However, the allegations have not been supported by medical records, identifiable witnesses or other independently verifiable evidence.In another post on Sunday, Xie claimed that Kim had suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage, fallen into a coma and been transferred to Beijing for emergency treatment. He alleged that a team of specialists from Peking Union Medical College Hospital had travelled to North Korea before Kim was moved to China."It is rumoured that recently, Kim Jong-un, General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and Supreme Leader of North Korea, suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage and fell into a coma. Although a team of medical experts from Peking Union Medical College Hospital was dispatched to North Korea to assist in his treatment, the poor medical conditions in North Korea forced Kim Jong-un to be transferred to Peking Union Medical College Hospital for emergency treatment. However, due to the severity of his condition and the fact that the optimal window for treatment had passed, Kim Jong-un succumbed to his injuries and died. His body has been secretly transported back to North Korea, and the news of his death is being kept under wraps."Xie further alleged that Kim's body had been secretly returned to North Korea and that authorities were concealing news of his death. He also claimed that Chinese troops had been deployed to Pyongyang amid fears of a succession crisis.In a separate post, he wrote: "It is said that on October 17, Peking Union Medical College Hospital dispatched a team of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular medical experts to North Korea to participate in the rescue of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, who was in critical condition."Xie's posts also fuelled speculation about a possible power struggle involving Kim's daughter, Kim Ju-ae, and his sister, Kim Yo Jong. He claimed that China had sent 9,000 troops to Pyongyang to help stabilise the situation.The claims of Kim's death, a Chinese troop deployment and a possible succession crisis remain unverified. North Korean authorities have not explicitly addressed the death reports.Kim's health has long been the subject of international speculation. The New York Post reported that South Korea's National Intelligence Service told lawmakers on September 30 that Kim weighed approximately 140 kilograms (309 pounds) and faced an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease because of severe obesity.However, the agency reportedly detected no significant signs of ill health, pointing to Kim's ability to run up stairs during an inspection of a naval destroyer.The latest rumours echo a false alarm in 2020, when Ji Seong-ho, a North Korean defector who later became a South Korean lawmaker, claimed he was "99%" certain that Kim had died following cardiovascular surgery. Kim subsequently appeared in public, and Ji apologised for making the erroneous claim.The New York Post said it had sought comment from the governments of North Korea and China, as well as Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
Article Summary: North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis. Unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.

Article Title: Typhoon Champi: Taiwan issues land warning, cancels 125 flights as powerful storm approaches
Article Text:
Nasa's Terra satellite shows Typhoon Noul in the Pacific Ocean, approaching Taiwan and Japan's main islands on its northward journey (Reuters image)

Taiwan issued a land warning for powerful Typhoon Champi on Thursday and cancelled 125 flights as the storm approached the island's northeastern coast, bringing the threat of destructive winds, torrential rain and waves exceeding six metres, Reuters reported.Champi, which was previously classified as a super typhoon, weakened slightly but continued to pack gusts of more than 227 kmph near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration. The storm was about 520 km southeast of Taiwan's southern tip and was expected to pass close to the northeastern coast late on Friday before moving north towards the Chinese coast.Taiwan President Lai Ching-te urged residents to prepare for the storm and avoid mountainous and coastal areas."A little more preparation means less risk," he wrote on his Facebook page.Mobile phone alerts warning of waves exceeding six metres were issued to coastal towns, while rainfall approaching one metre was forecast in northern mountainous areas, including hills near the capital Taipei. Weather experts warned that the storm's impact could last nearly two days.Taiwan's transport ministry said 125 flights had been cancelled on Thursday, mostly domestic services, while the rail network remained unaffected.The interior ministry said no evacuations had been reported.Champi is also forecast to pass over Yonaguni, Japan's westernmost inhabited island in Okinawa Prefecture. Japan Airlines, ANA and Skymark cancelled more than 100 flights between Thursday and Sunday, mostly domestic services, disrupting travel for more than 11,000 passengers.
Article Summary: Taiwan issues land warning for powerful Typhoon Champi. 125 flights cancelled as storm approaches island's northeastern coast. Threat of destructive winds, torrential rain and waves exceeding six metres. Japan Airlines, ANA and Skymark cancel more than 100 flights between Thursday and Sunday.

Article Title: Explosion, fuel leak: Two Syrian pipelines damaged in fresh blow to war-hit energy network
Article Text:
Security forces of Syria's Interior Ministry guard the al-Omar oil field, the country's largest by area and production

Two pipelines carrying gas and petroleum products were damaged in separate incidents in Syria on Thursday, with one explosion triggering a fire and another causing a fuel leak, Syrian state media reported.According to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA), citing the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Company, an explosion struck the Jbessa gas pipeline in Hasakah province, while a separate leak was detected on the Baniyas-Homs petroleum-products pipeline near Homs.The explosion struck the Jbessa gas export pipeline in the al-Arabidi area of Hasakah province, setting the pipeline on fire. Emergency teams isolated the damaged section and shut valves to contain the blaze.The Syrian Petroleum Company described the incident as sabotage. Officials said alternative arrangements would maintain gas supplies to power stations during repairs, while domestic gas supplies remained unaffected.In a separate incident, a hole was discovered in the Baniyas-Homs pipeline in the Hadida area west of Homs, causing a leak of petroleum products. Emergency and technical teams were deployed to contain the leak and isolate the damaged section.Al Jazeera, citing Syrian state media, reported that the damage to the Baniyas-Homs pipeline was believed to be linked to an attempted fuel theft. The initial reports did not confirm the cause or identify those responsible.The incidents come amid a series of disruptions to Syria’s energy infrastructure. Earlier in October, an oil pipeline near Tal Hamis in Hasakah province was damaged in what the Syrian Petroleum Company described as sabotage.Syria is working to rebuild its oil and gas infrastructure after years of conflict, restoring production in northeastern oilfields and reconnecting them with processing facilities and refineries in Homs and Baniyas.In January 2026, the Syrian Petroleum Company began pumping raw gas from the Jbessa fields in Hasakah to the Furqlus gas plant in Homs countryside at around 1.2 million cubic metres per day to support electricity generation.The second damaged pipeline, connecting Baniyas on the Mediterranean coast to Homs, transports petroleum products between two important energy centres. The Baniyas refinery is undergoing an overhaul aimed at increasing its processing capacity from around 80,000 to 130,000 barrels per day.Syria has also undertaken emergency pipeline repairs and plans to expand its transportation network. A September 2026 analysis by the Baker Institute for Public Policy reported that the Syrian Petroleum Company was repairing existing infrastructure and planning a heavy-crude pipeline linking northeastern oilfields to the Baniyas refinery.
Article Summary: Two pipelines carrying gas and petroleum products were damaged in separate incidents in Syria on Thursday. One explosion struck the Jbessa gas export pipeline in the al-Arabidi area of Hasakah province, setting the pipeline on fire. Emergency teams isolated the damaged section and shut valves to contain the blaze. A separate leak was detected on the Baniyas-Homs petroleum-products pipeline near Homs.

Article Title: Kylie Jenner launched a lip kit in 2015 and built a global cosmetics brand; Coty agreed to pay $600 million for a 51% stake in 2019
Article Text:
Image: Left/Britannica/Right/Refinery29

How the November 2015 Kylie Lip Kit launch became Kylie Cosmetics, a beauty brand with global reach

Kylie Cosmetics stand at Melbourne Airport, Australia. Image Credit: Wikipedia

Why Coty agreed to pay 600 million dollars for 51 per cent ownership of the Kylie Jenner partnership

Kylie Jenner arrives at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party on Sunday, March 15, 2026, at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art in LA.

177 million dollars in revenue, growth targets and the financial case for Coty

How creative control, licensing and Coty's manufacturing reach shaped the global beauty expansion plan

Where Coty stands today as a global beauty company and how the Kylie Jenner partnership fits its plans

Few beauty stories capture the power of social media as clearly as the rise of Kylie Jenner 's cosmetics business. What began in November 2015 as a debut lip kit became Kylie Cosmetics, a brand that built a devoted audience online and then attracted one of the largest beauty companies in the world. In November 2019, that company, Coty, agreed to buy a majority stake in the business for 600 million dollars. Here’s how the brand grew, what the agreement contained, why the numbers mattered, and how the partnership was designed to carry the business into new global markets. The deal also marked a turning point in the influencer-led beauty industry, demonstrating how a strong digital following could translate into a valuable global consumer brand.Coty's press release describes the origin story plainly. In November 2015, Kylie Jenner launched Kylie Cosmetics, and the debut product, the Kylie Lip Kit, was a sell-out success. Her online store, KylieCosmetics.com, is one of the most successful online stores in the world, and the range grew well beyond lips to include eyeliners, eyeshadows, blushes, highlighters, concealers, brushes and makeup bags, plus limited edition sets released throughout the year.In May 2019, she introduced Kylie Skin, a range of skincare products. The audience behind it was enormous, Coty says she has more than 270 million followers across her personal and brand social media channels, and that both brands are among the fastest-growing and most-engaged beauty brands on social media. Forbes featured her as the youngest-ever self-made billionaire in August 2018.On 18 November 2019, Coty and Kylie Jenner announced a long-term strategic partnership. Under the terms of the agreement, Coty would acquire 51 per cent ownership in the partnership for 600 million dollars, and the acquisition was expected to close in the third quarter of Coty's fiscal year 2020. Coty described the transaction as a key milestone in its ongoing transformation into a more focused and agile company. Chairman of the Board Peter Harf told the public that the partnership was an exciting step in Coty's renewed emphasis on its beauty business, calling Kylie Jenner a modern-day icon with an incredible sense of the beauty consumer. Pierre Laubies, Coty's chief executive officer, told the public the company was pleased to welcome her into its organisation and family.Coty's press release sets out the financial case in specific terms. Kylie Cosmetics generated an estimated 177 million dollars in net revenues over the preceding twelve months. Coty said it expected the transaction to add more than 1 per cent per year to the net revenue growth of its core fragrance, cosmetics and skin care portfolio over the next three years. The company also expected the deal to be neutral to its earnings per share in the first year and to add to them afterwards, and it expected the return on invested capital to exceed its cost of capital by fiscal year 2023. Tiger Shark served as an advisor to Coty on the transaction. Coty also scheduled a conference call that morning, with the live audio webcast and presentation slides made available through its investor relations website.The agreement divides responsibilities along each side's strengths. Together, Coty and Kylie Jenner set and lead the strategic direction, focusing on global expansion and entry into new beauty categories. Kylie Jenner and her team keep leading all creative efforts in product and communications, building on her global reach through social media. Coty takes overall responsibility for developing the portfolio, drawing on its knowledge of research and development, manufacturing, distribution and commercial strategy, and it acts as licensee for skincare, fragrances and nail products. All beauty categories continue to be sold through leading luxury beauty retailers and owned digital channels. Both parties aim to build what Coty calls a high-growth, digitally native beauty brand. Kylie Jenner told the public the partnership lets her team stay focused on creating and developing each product while building an international beauty powerhouse.Coty's own investor relations website shows the scale of the company that Kylie Jenner partnered with. Founded in Paris in 1904, Coty describes itself as one of the world's largest beauty companies, with a portfolio spanning fragrance, colour cosmetics, and skin and body care. The site lists the company as second globally in both fragrances and mass colour cosmetics, with more than 60 brands and licenses, about 11,300 employees, seven manufacturing sites and sales in more than 120 countries. For fiscal 2026, it reports net revenues of 5.8 billion dollars, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of 847 million dollars, and free cash flow of 348 million dollars. Pairing that infrastructure with a creator-led brand is what the partnership set out to do.
Article Summary: Coty and Kylie Jenner announced a long-term strategic partnership. Under the terms of the agreement, Coty would acquire 51 per cent ownership in the partnership for 600 million dollars. The acquisition was expected to close in the third quarter of Coty's fiscal year 2020. Both parties aim to build what Coty calls a high-growth beauty brand.

Article Title: In the 1950s, a Kentucky family bought 37 acres and later added a smaller access parcel; decades after the two were sold separately, new owners lost their court fight to use the neighbour's driveway
Article Text:
AI representation/ChatGPT

Two adjoining properties, sold separately

Why the couple said they needed the pathway

What the court said about an easement by necessity

Because Warinner and the surveyor testified that other access was available, the court found there was enough evidence to support the jury’s rejection of the claim.

Kentucky does not recognise a separate “apparent easement” theory

A property dispute in Kentucky has ended with a state appeals court ruling against a couple who claimed they had the right to use a neighbour’s pathway to reach their land. The dispute centred on two adjoining parcels that once belonged to the same family: a roughly 37-acre property bought in the 1950s and a smaller, three-fourths-acre tract acquired about 20 years later. For years, the family used a pathway across the smaller parcel to reach parts of the larger property. But after the two tracts were sold separately, the new owners disagreed over whether that access could continue.On October 23, 2026, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld a jury’s decision that Charlie E. Stearns and Kathy Stearns had no legal easement allowing them to cross the adjoining property owned by John Warinner and Betty Warinner. As reported by American legal website Law Justia, the court found that evidence supported the jury’s conclusion that the Stearnses did not have a legal right to use the route.According to Law Justia, John Warinner’s parents bought the larger tract, approximately 37 acres, in the 1950s. About two decades later, they purchased the adjoining smaller tract, measuring three-fourths of an acre. The parents used a pathway on the smaller parcel to reach portions of the larger property.However, John Warinner testified that his parents had also used alternative routes for about 20 years before buying the smaller tract.After his parents died, the two parcels were sold separately by a court-appointed Master Commissioner on the same day. The Stearnses purchased the larger tract, which adjoined land they already owned. The Warinners bought the smaller parcel. The Stearnses believed they were entitled to continue using the pathway across the smaller property. The Warinners disagreed and eventually put up barriers to prevent access.The disagreement led to a lawsuit in 2022. The Warinners accused the Stearnses of wrongly claiming an easement across their land and also brought a trespass claim against them. The case went to a jury trial in February 2025.The Stearnses argued that their right to use the route had developed while both parcels were under common ownership. Their claim relied on the idea that a property owner’s long-standing use of one part of a property to benefit another part can, in some circumstances, create an easement when ownership is later divided. They argued that the route was an implied easement, including an easement by necessity and what they described as an “apparent easement”.There was evidence supporting their position. Two of John Warinner’s sisters testified that the rough terrain made it extremely difficult, if not practically impossible, to reach the larger tract without crossing the smaller one. But other witnesses gave a different account. John Warinner said alternative access routes existed, and a surveyor testified that the Stearnses could reach the larger property without crossing the Warinners’ land.Warinner also identified an older road that could be used after repairs, although he acknowledged that it needed work before it would be usable. The appeals court said the evidence gave the jury a factual question to decide: whether crossing the smaller tract was reasonably necessary for access to the larger one.Under Kentucky law, an easement by necessity generally requires common ownership before the properties were divided, a subsequent separation of ownership and a strict need to use the neighbouring property to obtain access. The appeals court said an easement by necessity generally cannot be established if the landowner has another way to reach a public road, even if that alternative is inconvenient.Because Warinner and the surveyor testified that other access was available, the court found there was enough evidence to support the jury’s rejection of the claim. The court also considered the argument that the pathway qualified as a ‘quasi-easement.’ This legal concept can arise when an owner uses one part of a property to benefit another and the use is sufficiently established, apparent and reasonably necessary to the land.The judges said the Stearnses had to show more than a history of using the pathway. They needed to establish that the route was reasonably necessary to the enjoyment of the larger tract. Evidence of alternative access meant the jury could reasonably find that this requirement had not been met.The Stearnses also argued that the pathway qualified as an apparent easement, a separate category they said could justify their access. According to Law Justia, the Court of Appeals rejected that argument. The judges also rejected the couple’s suggestion that the jury’s brief deliberations indicated that it had ignored evidence or committed misconduct. They said there was no concrete evidence of improper conduct. The jury had found that the Stearnses trespassed, but awarded the Warinners no damages on that claim.The appeals court concluded that the evidence supported the jury’s verdict and affirmed the lower court’s judgment. The opinion was marked “not to be published”. The ruling leaves the Stearnses without the claimed legal right to use the pathway across the Warinners’ smaller parcel. It also underlines a key point in property disputes: a route used for years does not automatically become a legally enforceable easement when neighbouring properties are sold separately.
Article Summary: Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld a jury’s decision that Charlie E. Stearns and Kathy Stearn had no legal easement allowing them to cross the adjoining property. The dispute centred on two adjoining parcels that once belonged to the same family: a roughly 37-acre property bought in the 1950s and a smaller, three-fourths-acre tract acquired about 20 years later. For years, the family used a pathway across the smaller parcel to reach parts of the larger property. After the two tracts were sold separately, the new owners disagreed over whether that access could continue.

Article Title: Jensen Ackles and his family bought a 15-acre Texas ranch and turned it into a destination brewery; six years after opening, the public taproom closed but its beers continued reaching stores across Te
Article Text:
Despite his acting schedule, Ackles helped shape the brewery’s design, construction and constantly evolving beer selection.

From backyard brews to a Texas destination

More than just a brewery

A changing business model

For Jensen Ackles , the idea of a family business was already part of his professional mythology. After years of playing Dean Winchester on Supernatural, where family, loyalty and adventure formed the heart of the story, the actor brought a version of that ethos into real life. In Dripping Springs, Texas, Ackles, his wife Danneel and brother-in-law Gino Graul transformed a 15-acre property into Family Business Beer Co., a destination built around craft beer, food, music and community. What began as a backyard experiment eventually became a full-fledged brewery, although its journey has since taken a different direction. Scroll down read the details.The origins of Family Business Beer Co. were surprisingly informal. While living in California, Ackles and the Graul family began experimenting with a small brewing system that had been stored in the actor's backyard. Weekend brewing sessions gradually developed into a genuine passion, prompting Gino Graul to pursue formal brewing education, including studies at UC Davis and the Siebel Institute in Chicago, states a 2018 Forbes report.The family eventually brought the concept to Texas, where Ackles and Danneel had settled after moving to Austin in 2014.Construction on the Dripping Springs brewery began in 2017, turning their interest in craft beer into a substantial hospitality venture.According to Forbes, Ackles remained deeply involved in the project despite his demanding acting schedule, contributing to everything from design and construction details to testing the brewery's evolving selection of beers.According to Yahoo, when Family Business Beer Co. opened in January 2018, it was designed as an experience rather than simply a place to grab a drink. The sprawling property included a taproom, outdoor spaces, children's playground areas, games and a stage for live music.Food was also central to the concept. The property became home to Jep's Southern Roots, a food truck operated by Duck Dynasty personalities Jep and Jessica Robertson, bringing Southern comfort food and Cajun-inspired dishes into the mix. Local wines and non-alcoholic beverages ensured the destination's appeal beyond beer.As reported by Yahoo, the brewery was conceived around bringing people together through good beer, music and food, while its name offered a playful connection to Ackles' Supernatural legacy. "Family Business" echoed one of the show's most recognisable themes while also reflecting the venture's genuinely family-run foundation.At its peak, the brewery offered a constantly evolving lineup, with roughly 10 to 12 styles available at different times. Rather than relying on a fixed menu, the brewing team experimented with seasonal releases, rotating IPAs, lagers, ales and barrel-aged beers.But in May 2024, Family Business announced a major change. The Dripping Springs location would close to the public as the company shifted its focus towards distributing its beers across Texas, states the official website.The brewery said its products would continue to be available through local retailers, while its team would concentrate on strengthening relationships with on- and off-premise partners in Austin, San Antonio and Houston. Its seasonal beers and rotating IPA series also returned, including Supe Juice Hazy IPA, the website report claims.The evolution marks a new chapter for Family Business Beer Co. The destination taproom may have closed, but the family venture continues to carry its Texas identity into stores and markets across the state.Images Courtesy: istock and Instagram/jensenackles
Article Summary: Supernatural actor Jensen Ackles opened Family Business Beer Co. in Dripping Springs, Texas, in January 2018. The brewery was designed as an experience, with a taproom, outdoor spaces, children's playground areas, games and a stage for live music. The property became home to Jep's Southern Roots, a food truck operated by Duck Dynasty personalities Jep and Jessica Robertson. In May 2024, the brewery announced it would close its taproom and focus on distributing its beers across Texas.

Article Title: In 1996, a New York couple bought their home believing a tree line marked the boundary; 30 years later, an appeals court revived a privacy claim over cameras filming their backyard and daughter
Article Text:
Dalys built a chain-link fence in 2006, while Rileys installed their own fence about two feet away in 2011. (AI image)

Disagreement over trees led to surveillance cameras

Why court allowed privacy claim to continue

What happened to the original property dispute?

A New York couple who bought their home in 1996 believing that a line of trees marked the boundary with their neighbour's property have spent years fighting over the same stretch of land. What began as a disagreement over where one property ended and the other began eventually involved allegations of trespass and surveillance cameras recording their backyard.Nearly 30 years after the purchase, a New York appeals court has revived the couple's privacy claim after they alleged that their neighbours' cameras captured thousands of images and videos, including footage of their swimming pool and young daughter.According to details of the case available on Justia , the ruling, delivered on Thursday, concerns Timothy J. Riley and his co-plaintiff, who own a home in the Town of Malta, Saratoga County, and their neighbours, John C Daly and his co-defendant. Both properties are part of a four-plot residential development, with the Rileys living on the northern side and the Dalys to the south.The Rileys purchased their property from the developer in December 1996.At the time, they understood that the trees between the two plots marked the boundary. The original neighbour appeared to share that understanding. He watched them maintain the wooded area on their side and later helped them build a garage about 15 feet from the trees.Things began to change in 2004 when the neighbour sold his property to the Dalys. Two years later, the new owners built a chain-link fence between the tree line and the Rileys' garage. The Rileys believed the fence stood on their land. In 2011, they installed their own fence about two feet away. Over time, the disagreement grew into a dispute involving approximately 230 feet of the boundary.By 2018, the dispute had reached the courts. Both households accused each other of wrongdoing in the contested area. The Rileys wanted the boundary they had recognised for years to be legally accepted, while the Dalys maintained that the land belonged to them.But the disagreement was no longer limited to fences and property lines. The Dalys had also installed surveillance cameras, which became a major part of the Rileys' lawsuit.The Dalys told the court that they had installed the cameras to monitor their property following alleged incidents of trespass, theft and harassment. They maintained that the purpose was to prevent further problems, not to harass their neighbours.The Rileys, however, raised concerns about what the cameras were recording. They submitted photographs showing their backyard and swimming pool, including an image of their daughter, who was a minor.They also claimed that information obtained from one of the cameras and during the legal proceedings showed that thousands of photographs or videos had been captured. According to them, the recordings extended beyond the disputed strip of land into other parts of their backyard.New York has a law that protects homeowners against certain types of unwanted surveillance by neighbours. It allows people to seek damages if cameras are installed on adjoining property to record activities in their backyard without written permission and with the intention of harassing, alarming or threatening them.The lower court had earlier dismissed their privacy claim. However, the appeals court disagreed, finding that the photographs and allegations about the recordings raised questions that needed further examination and reinstated the Rileys' invasion of privacy claim.While the cameras became an important issue, the question that started the disagreement remained unresolved: Where exactly was the boundary between the two homes?The Rileys argued that the tree line should be recognised because it had been treated as the boundary for years. Under New York law, a boundary accepted by neighbouring owners for more than 10 years can, in certain circumstances, become legally recognised.However, the court found that the Rileys had not provided enough evidence to establish that both households had accepted the trees as the boundary for the required period. The Dalys' decision to build a fence on the Rileys' claimed side of the trees also raised doubts about such an agreement.The Dalys, meanwhile, relied on land surveys to support their ownership claim. But the Rileys pointed out differences between the surveys, arguing that these could shift the boundary by approximately 10 feet.They also alleged that wooden survey stakes and the original natural boundary had been removed before a surveyor inspected the property in 2018.The appeals court found that these differences could not be ignored. It thus overturned the lower court's decision to settle the boundary according to the Dalys' survey.Another disagreement involved allegations that the Rileys had cut or removed trees from the disputed land. The judges found that this issue also required further examination because ownership of the area had not been conclusively established.
Article Summary: New York couple bought their home in 1996 believing that a line of trees marked the boundary with their neighbour's property. The Rileys wanted the boundary they had recognised for years to be legally accepted, while the Dalys maintained that the land belonged to them. Over time, the disagreement grew into a dispute involving approximately 230 feet of the boundary. Both households accused each other of wrongdoing in the contested area. The Dalys had also installed surveillance cameras, which became a major part of the lawsuit.

Article Title: Nebraska workers cut 150 trees from crowded lake banks and sank them at 16 underwater locations; the September 2026 project is building shelter for young fish in two lakes without using concrete reefs
Article Text:
How trees become underwater fish shelters

Clearing crowded banks improves fishing access

Part of a wider habitat restoration effort

Can the new habitat help fish populations?

Instead of building concrete reefs, conservation workers in Nebraska have turned trees cleared from overgrown lake banks into underwater fish habitats, placing around 150 trees at 16 locations across two lakes. The project, completed in September 2026, aims to give smaller fish places to hide from predators while improving fishing access along the shore. According to the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission, the trees were transported and submerged using a new Aquatic Habitat Barge at Bridgeport State Recreation Area.The project used approximately 60 cedar and Russian olive trees at five locations in the recreation area's southeast lake and another 90 trees at 11 locations in the middle lake. The trees were removed from crowded shoreline areas, allowing crews to address two problems at once: overgrown banks that restricted access for anglers and a shortage of underwater woody habitat for fish.The commission announced the work on October 22, explaining that the brush piles would provide shelter for smaller fish and help support the aquatic food web. The project is part of Nebraska's wider effort to improve lake habitats and make fishing more productive.Trees that might otherwise be removed as shoreline vegetation can serve another purpose once submerged. Their branches and trunks create a network of spaces where small fish can hide, making it harder for larger predatory fish to reach them. The underwater structures also provide surfaces where algae and other organisms can grow. These can attract plankton and small aquatic creatures, which in turn become food for fish. The resulting chain of interactions helps support a wider aquatic food web.The Nebraska Game and Parks Commission said the brush piles are intended to benefit fish populations and anglers by improving habitat conditions. However, the announcement does not provide post-project monitoring data demonstrating a measured increase in fish numbers at the two lakes. The trees are not simply dumped into the water at random. Crews transport and position them at selected underwater locations, while the commission makes approximate placement information available through its lake habitat and structure maps. These help anglers identify underwater features that may attract fish.The project also illustrates how vegetation removed for one practical reason can be reused to address a different environmental need.The work has a benefit beyond the underwater ecosystem. The cedar and Russian olive trees were cut from overgrown shoreline areas, opening up sections of the banks for anglers. Shoreline vegetation can restrict access to the water, particularly at locations where trees and branches have grown densely. Removing selected trees can make it easier for people to reach the water's edge while allowing some of the same material to be reused as fish habitat.Bridgeport State Recreation Area, located in western Nebraska, covers approximately 326 acres, including 78 acres of water spread across five sandpit lakes. The area offers fishing, boating, camping, swimming and other outdoor activities, according to the state agency. Its waters support several fish species, including largemouth bass, walleye, bluegill, yellow perch and channel catfish. Rainbow trout are also stocked in some of the area's lakes. Improving underwater habitat can help fisheries managers maintain suitable conditions for fish while making recreational waters more useful to visitors.Nebraska has been using a range of approaches to improve aquatic habitats, including submerged trees, artificial fish attractors and rock structures. The Nebraska Game and Parks Commission's Aquatic Habitat Program was established in 1997. According to the agency, it has generated more than $90 million for improvements to 137 water bodies across the state. The programme supports projects intended to improve aquatic conditions, fisheries and recreational access.A 2026 overview published by Nebraskaland Magazine, the commission's outdoor publication, describes other efforts involving woody habitat. At 11 lakes along Interstate 80, invasive eastern red cedar and Russian olive trees were removed to improve shoreline access, with some of the cut trees placed in the lakes to create fish habitat.The state has also used rock shoals at other reservoirs. In partnership with the US Bureau of Reclamation, 42 shoals were built at Medicine Creek Reservoir in 2025, following the construction of 43 at Swanson Reservoir in 2023. These structures provide underwater habitat in areas that otherwise offer relatively few features for fish.The different projects show that habitat restoration does not depend on a single design. Depending on the water body and its needs, managers can use woody material, rocks or purpose-built structures to increase habitat diversity. The Bridgeport project specifically uses trees rather than newly constructed rock structures. However, the commission has not described it as a formal replacement for concrete reefs, and the wider state programme continues to use other habitat-building methods where appropriate.The immediate objective is to create places where smaller fish can escape predators and where food organisms can gather. Such structures can make underwater environments more complex, providing fish with shelter and feeding opportunities that may be scarce in open areas.The commission expects the improved habitat to support healthier fish populations and better fishing opportunities. Whether the new brush piles produce a measurable increase in fish abundance at Bridgeport will depend on factors including water conditions, food availability, predation and the long-term use of the structures by different species.The state has made the approximate locations of the newly installed brush piles available through its lake contour and habitat maps, allowing anglers to find the underwater structures.For now, the September project offers a practical example of how clearing overgrown shorelines can do more than improve access. By placing the cut trees beneath the water, Nebraska's fisheries managers have converted vegetation into a resource intended to support fish, aquatic food webs and recreational fishing.
Article Summary: Trees were removed from overgrown shoreline areas at two lakes in Nebraska. They were submerged to provide underwater habitat for fish. The project is part of a wider effort to improve lake habitats and make fishing more productive. The state has also used rock shoals at other reservoirs.

Article Title: ‘Largest ever’: Elon Musk donates $443 million to Trump's campaign ahead of US midterms
Article Text:
The largest share of the PAC's spending has gone towards the Texas Senate race (Photo: Reuters).

Texas senate race gets largest share of spending

Billionaire Elon Musk has spent more than $442 million on Republican campaigns and political groups ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, emerging as the largest individual political donor in US history.Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings show that Musk made three direct contributions totalling $74.8 million to his America PAC between October 6 and 14, Forbes reported. An additional $1.98 million came through his company, United States of America Inc., taking his total contributions for the first half of October to nearly $77 million.America PAC is a political action committee founded and heavily backed by Musk to support Republican and conservative candidates through voter turnout operations and digital campaigns.According to Forbes, America PAC reported spending approximately $42.7 million during the first two weeks of October, with $46.5 million in cash remaining as of October 14.The PAC has reported around $68.6 million in independent expenditures during the current midterm election cycle, primarily targeting competitive Senate races, according to FEC records compiled by the PaidForPolitics tracker.The largest share of the PAC's spending has gone towards the Texas Senate race.It has spent $27.9 million opposing Democratic candidate James Talarico and another $4.8 million supporting his Republican opponent, Ken Paxton. Forbes reported.America PAC has also spent approximately $9.3 million on the Ohio Senate race, followed by $7.7 million in Michigan, $2.7 million in Iowa and $2.1 million in Maine. The spending in these states has primarily focused on opposing Democratic candidates.Earlier this month, The New York Times reported that Musk had contributed more than $366 million to midterm election races by the end of September, including donations to America PAC and other outside groups.That figure included a $158 million donation to the Republican Senate Leadership Fund last month. The super PAC subsequently transferred an identical amount to the Texas PAC, which supports Paxton's campaign.Forbes estimated Musk's net worth at $909.8 billion as of late Thursday night, retaining his position as the world's richest person.
Article Summary: Musk made three direct contributions totalling $74.8 million to his America PAC between October 6 and 14. An additional $1.98 million came through his company, taking his total contributions for the first half of October to nearly $77 million. America PAC is a political action committee founded and heavily backed by Musk to support Republican candidates.

Article Title: In 2017, after Cyclone Debbie damaged reefs, marine biologist Johnny Gaskell searched Google Maps for blue holes; divers found one 150 metres wide that may have sheltered coral from the storm
Article Text:
Marine biologist Johnny Gaskell discovered a massive 150-meter-wide blue hole in the Great Barrier Reef using satellite imagery on Google Maps. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

How Gaskell used Google Maps satellite view after Cyclone Debbie in 2017

The dive about five months later: a hole 150 metres across and at least 20 metres deep

Seriatopora

Acropora

Earlier geological work on blue holes in the Pompey hard line reefs

Staghorn coral (Acropora). Gaskell reported large, delicate staghorn and birdsnest colonies inside the blue hole about five months after Cyclone Debbie. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

How uneven Cyclone Debbie’s damage was across Whitsunday reefs

Report on surveys of the Whitsundays sector of the Great Barrier Reef

Tropical cyclones can break apart branching corals and strip reef flats and the damage differs from one reef to the next depending on depth, exposure and the path of the storm. In 2017, marine biologist Johnny Gaskell, working from the Whitsunday region in Queensland, searched for areas where coral could have survived Cyclone Debbie. He used the satellite view in Google Maps to locate blue holes, which are deep circular structures that appear as dark spots in the lighter water of the lagoon surrounding them. Gaskell dived into one of the spots and said he found large, fragile colonies of coral that had survived the cyclone. Most of what is known about the find comes from his own observations and from reports of them.Google’s Maps blog says Gaskell used satellite view in 2017 to trace Cyclone Debbie’s path and pinpoint areas along the reef that may have been spared from damage. There he spotted perfect circles, indicating a possible blue hole, in the Hard Line Reefs south of the Whitsundays, a difficult-to-reach area that is dangerous to navigate. The blog adds that only two blue holes had been documented in the Great Barrier Reef until a few years earlier and describes Gaskell and a team of researchers as finding previously unknown ones, although Gaskell wrote in an Instagram post that geologists had already described and documented the hole he dived and said his team may well have been the first to dive it.The team then used satellite view on their phones to steer through narrow channels in unsurveyed waters until the blue dot sat over the hole.In that post, quoted by Australian Geographic, Gaskell wrote that a category 4 cyclone had gone straight over the area just five months before the dive. At depths of 15 to 20 metres, he saw huge birdsnest corals () and very elongated staghorn corals (), which he described as among the biggest and most delicate colonies he had seen. He suggested that their survival was a result of the hole’s position within the lagoon walls. SBS reports that Gaskell could explore the hole for only about an hour at high tide, when conditions were safest and measured it at 150 metres across and at least 20 metres deep, adding that it needed another visit to establish its true depth. National Geographic later reported the hole as just shy of 100 feet deep at its centre, or roughly 30 metres. The same post, as quoted by ZME Science, places the hole over 200 kilometres from Daydream Island, in one of the least explored parts of the reef. Gaskell’s explanation of the hole’s protective effect is his own interpretation.The 1979 study Drowned dolines: the blue holes of the Pompey Reefs, Great Barrier Reef describes two blue holes at Cockatoo and Molar Reefs in the Pompey hard line reefs. They are roughly circular, between 240 and 295 metres across and 30 to 40 metres deep. The record’s summary says the holes are collapsed dolines that may have taken more than one period of low sea level to form. The paper adds that both features were mapped in detail during an October 1977 expedition using echo-profiling, scuba exploration, sediment coring, seismic refraction and shallow drilling. Cockatoo is completely rimmed by living coral, while Molar is only partly rimmed and seismic refraction across the rims revealed a shallow pre-Holocene surface 8.5 to 11 metres beneath them.The record also says the inner slopes include sediment fans and terraces at depth. This fits what Gaskell told National Geographic: blue holes can be like time capsules for the ocean because sediment builds up in them over thousands of years. In his post, Gaskell said geologists had mentioned the craters before, but the sources do not say whether this is one of those two features or whether it is smaller. The Australian Institute of Marine Science published the, covering four reefs surveyed after the cyclone. This clearly shows the uneven distribution of damage. There are two outer shelf reefs that have seen an increase in hard coral cover since 2017, which suggests little damage. Reefs in the outer Whitsundays showed high, diverse coral cover with little evidence of cyclonic damage.In the study, two surveys on four reefs found a sector-wide median hard coral cover of 10-30%, with no crown-of-thorns starfish recorded and only low, scattered bleaching on half the reefs surveyed. The paper also notes a stark contrast between sites: Hayman Island fell from 37% coral cover to 5% after Cyclone Debbie, while the outer-shelf reefs Rebe and Slate Reef showed increases from 2017 levels. This patchy pattern allows for the existence of a sheltered area, but does not give an explanation for it. Gaskell has said he will not disclose the location of the hole because an influx of divers would severely damage colonies he described as more delicate than usual.
